report.code_assessment: The code follows the spec closely. Most files read like direct translations of their scopes, with the same wording in comments, labels, tooltips and behaviour, and many spec details show up nearly word for word: the divergence panel, folder browser, git panel, settings window, scrollbar, ribbon, and prompt mode's queue, history and answer drawer. Almost all of the drift is the implementation filling in details the spec leaves open: scoring weights, refresh intervals, model choices, widths, the harness's command-line flags, and workarounds for gpui-kit. A few things are added that no spec mentions, such as formatting Piton on save, an 80-column minimum editor width, a saved `mode` property in the hidden anchor, and a markdown workaround. The spec is contradicted only in small ways: the palette labels its command "Build Spec" where the spec says "Build", the activity list is in a fixed order rather than newest last, a failed build still shows a tick in the divergence steps, and a few module comments are out of date. Some files have no spec behind them at all, mostly infrastructure: bootstrap, the LSP transport, markdown fixes, and fuzzy scoring.
report.spec_assessment: The UI and feature scopes are unusually complete and exact: they give labels, key bindings, colours, sizes, thresholds, file locations and edge cases, and the code follows them almost line for line. Most strings in the spec appear verbatim in the source, and the constants match (drawer share 0.8 within 0.2 to 0.95, 12 input rows, a 400-file cap, a 32px inset, a 260px sidebar that can't go below 160). Only a few small differences remain. Git state is read separately by each view that shows it. The Chain prompt file is named combined.md rather than after its tab. The activity list minimizes the divergence panel where the spec says it closes it. The quit dialog only says generically that a prompt is running. The spec is thinner and more abstract at the top: the meta-model, the agent skill and command templates, project directory picking and harness integration. That is where an implementation has to guess.

well_defined.name: Chat input and answer drawer
well_defined.why: The tabs, Chain animation, tints, help text, attachments, grow-to-fit, drawer sizing, dimming and selection popover are all described in enough detail to build without guessing.

well_defined.name: Folder browser and New Project
well_defined.why: Validation messages, keyboard shortcuts per platform, config file contents, .gitignore contents and what is never overwritten are all spelled out.

well_defined.name: Git panel and git state
well_defined.why: The statuses and their order of priority, colours, commit message format, pull that refuses conflicts, and commit notes are each described precisely.

well_defined.name: Scrollbar and ribbon
well_defined.why: Layout, lock behaviour, the pulse animation, group title strips, opening several tabs, collapsing and the activity list are described with concrete sizes and rules.

well_defined.name: Settings window and system prompts
well_defined.why: Window size, title, file locations, placeholders, reset behaviour and baked-in defaults are all given explicitly.

well_defined.name: Prompt mode and chat input
well_defined.why: Tabs, tints, queue, history, the Ask stack, the answer drawer, attachments and the hidden anchor are all specified down to wording, percentages and persistence paths, and the code matches.

well_defined.name: Ribbon and its tabs
well_defined.why: Each tab is its own scope naming its groups, commands, icons, tooltips, primary flags and disabled states, and the ribbon module is split to match.

well_defined.name: Reusable UI components
well_defined.why: The scrollbar, diff view, folder browser, inset panel and git panel spell out layout, keyboard behaviour, states and edge cases, including platform-specific shortcuts.

well_defined.name: New Project
well_defined.why: Validation rules, defaults, the generated piton.config.pi structure, the .gitignore contents and what never gets overwritten are all stated explicitly.

less_defined.name: Application bootstrap and platform glue
less_defined.why: ApplicationScope only names the stack and platforms, so app.rs, main.rs, asset loading and quitting when the last window closes are all the implementation's own choices.

less_defined.name: LSP transport and hidden-anchor serialization
less_defined.why: The spec names the protocol messages, but framing, request ids, answering the server, the anchor's source layout, and how piton.config.pi is parsed are left to the code.

less_defined.name: Harness invocation details
less_defined.why: The spec says auto mode, stdin and resuming, but the stream-json parsing, session-snapshot flag, built-in agent list, and the small model and effort used for commit notes and messages are filled in by the code.

less_defined.name: Fuzzy ranking and shell command layout
less_defined.why: The palette and message list describe what should rank higher and where commands split, but not the weights, thresholds or parsing rules.

less_defined.name: Editor extras
less_defined.why: Formatting Piton on save, the 80-column minimum width, and extension aliases beyond the listed ones aren't in the Editor scope.

less_defined.name: Rendering workarounds
less_defined.why: markdown.rs and several layout measurements exist to work around gpui-kit limits that no spec talks about.

less_defined.name: Spec meta-model and agent skills
less_defined.why: Concept, Shape and Scope are bare abstract anchors, and the BuildScope templates rely on a Belay shape root the project doesn't have, with slips such as using the command itself as the skill it should use.

less_defined.name: Harness integration
less_defined.why: It says auto mode, stdin input, streaming and session carry-over but not which harness is used or how, the output format, or what happens when the harness is missing, so the code hardcodes claude and adds unstated flags.

less_defined.name: Project directory
less_defined.why: A three-sentence scope that leaves out wrong-file handling, where the picker starts, and how switching projects resets what's open.

less_defined.name: Git awareness
less_defined.why: It describes a single source of git state and a refresh within a couple of seconds but not the mechanism, so each consumer polls git on its own.

less_defined.name: Application shape
less_defined.why: The projectFiles list leaves out system prompts, commit notes and divergence reports that other scopes save under .suspense, and the platforms get no platform-specific guidance.
